title: Restricted Fourier weight estimate error
statement: Let $n>0$, and let $\varepsilon=a/b$ be specified by positive integers $a,b$ with $2a\le b$. Let $s\ge1$ be an integer, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ have Fourier $1$-norm at most $s$. For any coordinate set $J$ and any subset $S$ of its indices, the absolute difference between the restricted Fourier weight estimate and its outer mean is at most $3\varepsilon/4$.
hypotheses_covered: The Fourier bound $s$ is an integer with $s\ge1$
The target is a sign-valued function on $\{−1,1\}^n$
$J$ is a subset of the coordinate indices
caveat: The restricted weight estimate and outer mean are algorithmically defined in the supplied context, whose informal descriptions are stubs; their full constructions are not restated here.
